deploy.title: Set the services' own credentials
deploy.instructions:
The services the stack runs use these credentials. Unless `secrets.env` sets them, they are fixed development values, the same in every environment.

| Credential | Name in `secrets.env` |
| --- | --- |
| Postgres superuser password | `LOCAL_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` |
| RustFS root access key | `LOCAL_RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY` |
| RustFS root secret key | `LOCAL_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY` |

To replace them with random ones, add them to `secrets.env` and render again. Rendering writes each value into every file that uses it (`.env`, `modules/*/.env/`, `modules/*/secrets/`):

```bash
cat >> secrets.env <<EOF
LOCAL_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
LOCAL_RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 10)
LOCAL_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 20)
EOF
trestle env render .
```

Do this before the first start. Services keep the credentials they first started with in their persisted data (under the data root, `.data/` by default), so a later change also needs that data removed, or the credential changed inside the service.

deploy.title: Start the stack
deploy.instructions:
Start every service and wait until each one is healthy:

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait
```

The gateway then serves the stack at <http://localhost:8080>. [LAYOUT.md](LAYOUT.md) lists every route and address.

deploy.title: Create the buckets
deploy.instructions:
Create the buckets the stack uses: `unity`, through the S3-compatible API at `${AWS_ENDPOINT_URL}`.
The script needs the AWS CLI, signed in with credentials that may create buckets (a profile,
SSO, or keys). Set `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` to a
key that may read and write them.
deploy.commands:
region='us-east-1'
endpoint=(--endpoint-url "${AWS_ENDPOINT_URL}")
for bucket in 'unity' ; do
  if aws s3api head-bucket --bucket "$bucket" ${endpoint[@]+"${endpoint[@]}"} 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "bucket $bucket exists"
  elif [ "$region" = us-east-1 ]; then
    aws s3api create-bucket --bucket "$bucket" --region "$region" \
      ${endpoint[@]+"${endpoint[@]}"} >/dev/null
    echo "created bucket $bucket"
  else
    aws s3api create-bucket --bucket "$bucket" --region "$region" \
      --create-bucket-configuration "LocationConstraint=$region" \
      ${endpoint[@]+"${endpoint[@]}"} >/dev/null
    echo "created bucket $bucket"
  fi
done

deploy.title: Create the Neon project
deploy.instructions:
Create a Neon project for the stack's databases. The script needs
[`neonctl`](https://neon.tech/docs/reference/neon-cli), signed in (`neonctl auth`, or
`NEON_API_KEY` set), and `jq`. It creates the project `trestle-uc-hybrid` unless it exists
(in `NEON_REGION`, default `aws-us-east-2`), then saves its id as `NEON_PROJECT_ID` and its connection details as `PGHOST`, `PGUSER`, `PGPASSWORD` in `secrets.env`.
deploy.commands:
project_name='trestle-uc-hybrid'
project_id="${NEON_PROJECT_ID:-}"
if [ -z "$project_id" ]; then
  project_id="$(neonctl projects list --output json \
    | jq -r --arg name "$project_name" '(.projects // .)[] | select(.name == $name) | .id' \
    | head -n 1)"
fi
if [ -z "$project_id" ]; then
  project_id="$(neonctl projects create --name "$project_name" \
    --region-id "${NEON_REGION:-aws-us-east-2}" --output json | jq -r '.project.id // .id')"
  echo "created Neon project $project_name ($project_id)"
else
  echo "Neon project $project_name exists ($project_id)"
fi
save_secret NEON_PROJECT_ID "$project_id"

# The project's default role and its password, from its connection string.
uri="$(neonctl connection-string --project-id "$project_id")"
rest="${uri#*://}"
credentials="${rest%%@*}"
host="${rest#*@}"
host="${host%%/*}"
host="${host%%:*}"
save_secret 'PGHOST' "$host"
save_secret 'PGUSER' "${credentials%%:*}"
save_secret 'PGPASSWORD' "${credentials#*:}"

deploy.title: Create the databases
deploy.instructions:
Create the databases the stack uses: `unitycatalog`. The script adds each one missing to the Neon project
`NEON_PROJECT_ID` with `neonctl`.
deploy.commands:
: "${NEON_PROJECT_ID:?set NEON_PROJECT_ID, or run the project step first}"
existing="$(neonctl databases list --project-id "$NEON_PROJECT_ID" --output json \
  | jq -r '(.databases // .)[] | .name')"
for db in 'unitycatalog' ; do
  if printf '%s\n' "$existing" | grep -qx "$db"; then
    echo "database $db exists"
  else
    neonctl databases create --project-id "$NEON_PROJECT_ID" --name "$db" --output json >/dev/null
    echo "created database $db"
  fi
done

deploy.title: Supply the hosted resources' secrets
deploy.instructions:
The hosted resources read `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `PGHOST`, `PGPASSWORD`, `PGUSER`. Set them in `secrets.env` beside `env.toml` (git-ignored; the scripts above save what they create there) or export them, then render again so the stack picks them up:

```bash
trestle env render .
```

deploy.title: Start the stack
deploy.instructions:
Start every service and wait until each one is healthy:

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait
```

Each service is then published on its own host port. [LAYOUT.md](LAYOUT.md) lists every route and address.

uc-hybrid.deploy-setup:
# Secrets kept in secrets.env (git-ignored) are read like exported ones.
if [ -f secrets.env ]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . ./secrets.env
  set +a
fi

# save_secret NAME VALUE: record NAME in secrets.env (and this shell), unless secrets.env
# already sets it.
save_secret() {
  if [ -f secrets.env ] && grep -q "^$1=" secrets.env; then
    echo "secrets.env already sets $1; leaving it as is"
  else
    (umask 077 && printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> secrets.env)
    echo "saved $1 to secrets.env"
  fi
  export "$1=$2"
}
